meta.title: Three-Dimensional-Bioprinted Embedded-Based Cerebral Organoids: An Alternative Approach for Mini-Brain In Vitro Modeling Beyond Conventional Generation Methods.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: iPSC-derived embryoid bodies were printed in an alginate/carboxymethylcellulose ink with diluted Matrigel to grow cerebral organoids without manual Matrigel embedding. The organoids reached ~2 mm by day 40, like standard ones.

formulations.name: 1.5% alginate + 1% CMC + Matrigel (1:10)
formulations.composition_detail: 1.5% w/v sodium alginate, 1% w/v sodium carboxymethylcellulose, Matrigel diluted 1:10
formulations.cell_type: neural embryoid bodies to cerebral organoids
formulations.key_outcome: Printed organoids grew to ~2 mm by day 40, matching Matrigel-embedded organoids with far less Matrigel.

evidence.quote: the Matrigel® is diluted (1:10) in a solution enriched with 1.5 w/v% sodium alginate (SA), 1 w/v% of sodium carboxymethylcellulose (CMC)
The experimental parameters used for the extrusion printing were a pressure of 0.4 bar, a speed of 100 mm/s, and a needle diameter of 0.6 mm
By day 40, these organoids reached approximately 2 mm in diameter, matching the size observed at the same time point in Matrigel®-based cORGs.
